Your stream.
Your tiny science lab.

A real paper-helicopter drop becomes an audience prediction. This lab includes three recorded trials, a read-only Twitch chat connection and an OBS overlay.

Try a recorded round ↗

Try the whole flow in a minute

  1. Keep The first drop and the 1.00-second prediction line.
  2. Choose Open predictions, then make a Yes or No practice prediction. Sample voters are optional and always labelled.
  3. Choose Lock predictions. The question and predictions can no longer change.
  4. Choose Play the drop. After it ends, choose Reveal reviewed result.
  5. Inspect the release and landing frames. Export the experiment to keep its evidence and prediction record.

The second trial uses a 1.20-second line inside its reviewed range. It demonstrates Too close to call. The third trial settles below its default 1.20-second line.

Connect your Twitch community

  1. Enter your channel name and select Connect. Wait for CONNECTED.
  2. Open a round. Viewers type !drop yes or !drop no in your channel's Twitch chat.
  3. Each Twitch user gets one prediction. Their latest valid command replaces the earlier choice until the host locks the round.
  4. After the reveal, viewers can propose the next test with !test blades, !test weight or !test repeat.

DropLab reads public chat using Twitch's IRC WebSocket connection. It sends connection and keepalive messages, but never posts chat messages. A successful chat connection is distinct from a verified broadcast.

Actual Twitch votes are labelled Twitch. Practice choices and sample voters remain separate in the interface and export. No audience numbers are invented.

If a connected chat feed drops during an open round, the studio locks predictions. Reconnect before starting another live round.

Add DropLab to OBS

For an OBS Browser source, run the local host on the same computer as OBS. Use Node.js 22 or newer.

npm start
  1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8768 and connect your channel.
  2. Select Open stream overlay and copy the URL.
  3. In OBS, add a Browser source at 1280 × 720 and paste the URL.
  4. Keep the studio open. Use its controls to open, lock and reveal each round. The overlay follows automatically.

The hosted demo can synchronize a second tab in the same browser. A separate OBS browser process needs the local host. Restarting the server ends its in-memory sessions; export before stopping it.

What the measurements mean

The supplied videos show real drops with handheld camera movement. The first color tracker could confuse the paper with the room background. These rounds use manual frame-review windows.

The flight-time range spans the earliest plausible landing minus the latest plausible release, through the latest plausible landing minus the earliest plausible release. It includes uncertainty in selecting the frames. Thirty frames per second does not establish measurement accuracy.

  • Yes: the entire reviewed range is at or above the prediction line.
  • No: the entire range is below it.
  • Too close to call: the range crosses the line. No side wins.

The clips were shortened around the drop and their audio removed. Speed is unchanged unless you select slow replay for inspection. All three use the same helicopter; they do not establish a design-performance difference. Next-test votes are proposals, not completed experiments.

Keep the evidence

Export experiment downloads JSON with the question, labelled predictions, a SHA-256 digest of the locked prediction payload, clip hashes, review windows and next-test votes. Recompute the digest to check the exported payload. This is an inspectable local record, not an independent timestamp or external notarization.

The overlay shows aggregate counts. The host export includes prediction display names and identifiers. Export what you intend to share. DropLab doesn't collect email addresses or ask for a Twitch password.

Test the code

npm ci
npm test
npm run check
npm run test:browser

Browser tests use Chrome on macOS if installed. Elsewhere, install Playwright Chromium with npx playwright install chromium. Tests cover the round flow, uncertain results, synchronized overlays, mobile layout and export verification.

The camera prototype is retained for tracking experiments. It is separate from this demo's manually reviewed timing.
